question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2{x}^{2}+1.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(2{x}^{2}+1\right)=4 x
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(2,9):$

$$
m=f'(2)=8
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=- \frac{1}{8}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-\left(9\right)&=- \frac{1}{8}\left(x-\left(2\right)\right) \\ x+8\cdot y&=74.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{7 x^{3} \left(x^{3} - 14\right)}{4}.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{7 x^{3} \left(x^{3} - 14\right)}{4}\right)=\frac{21 x^{2} \left(x^{3} - 7\right)}{2}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(4,5600):$

$$
m=f'(4)=9576
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=- \frac{1}{9576}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-\left(5600\right)&=- \frac{1}{9576}\left(x-\left(4\right)\right) \\ x+9576\cdot y&=53625604.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the equation of the normal line to the curve $y=16 x^{2} + 8$ at the point $(4,264).$

$x\,+$
{{field-1}}$\cdot \,y\,=$
{{field-2}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=16 x^{2} + 8.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(16 x^{2} + 8\right)=32 x
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(4,264):$

$$
m=f'(4)=128
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=- \frac{1}{128}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-\left(264\right)&=- \frac{1}{128}\left(x-\left(4\right)\right) \\ x+128\cdot y&=33796.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{33 \sqrt[3]{x}}{2}.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{33 \sqrt[3]{x}}{2}\right)=\frac{11}{2 x^{\frac{2}{3}}}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(8,33):$

$$
m=f'(8)=\frac{11}{8}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=- \frac{8}{11}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-\left(33\right)&=- \frac{8}{11}\left(x-\left(8\right)\right) \\ 8x+11\cdot y&=427.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the equation of the normal line to the curve $y=\frac{69 \sqrt[3]{x}}{2}$ at the point $(1,\frac{69}{2}).$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=\frac{69 \sqrt[3]{x}}{2}.$ First, we compute the derivative:

$$
f'(x)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\left(\frac{69 \sqrt[3]{x}}{2}\right)=\frac{23}{2 x^{\frac{2}{3}}}
$$

Then, we compute the slope of the tangent at the point $(1,\frac{69}{2}):$

$$
m=f'(1)=\frac{23}{2}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the normal line is

$$
m'=-\frac{1}{m}=- \frac{2}{23}.
$$

Finally, the equation of the normal line is

$$
\begin{aligned}y-\left(\frac{69}{2}\right)&=- \frac{2}{23}\left(x-\left(1\right)\right) \\ 8x+92\cdot y&=3182.\end{aligned}
$$
